action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is solid, and this is the kind of phase in which spending to win new and returning users has historically paid back best, especially among active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price has spent seven days just under its 50-day average and the Fed decides today, the sensible way to apply it is in steps: add spend gradually, review weekly, and speed up once price wins back about $81,899. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC is about 10% above its 200-day average ($73,069), which is still rising.
Up about 25% over 90 days; about 79% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But price ($80,738) has closed under its 50-day average ($81,899) for seven days.
Price swings are among the calmest in years, with the Fed deciding today.
watch: Price swings are about as calm as they have been in years while about two bets on a rise are open for every bet on a fall, and the Fed announces its decision today, 28 October. A close back above $81,899 would ease that tension; a close below $80,151 would turn the week down, and below $77,366 a drop signal would start.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still points up, but the last week has been soft. Short term, the picture is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed below its 50-day average for seven days (about 1% under it) and sits about 7% below its 30-day high, while the mood reading is a flat 51 and day-to-day swings are among the calmest in years. A close above $81,899 (the 50-day average) turns the week clearly up, a close below $80,151 (the 30-day low) turns it down, and in between it stays choppy, inside a typical week's swing of about $2,700. The Fed's decision today (28 October) and a large batch of Bitcoin options expiring on Friday (cryptoticker) are the dates to watch; hold big pushes until one side breaks.

Over the next month, the read is mixed. The three-month numbers still look good: price is about 25% above three months ago and about four in five of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average, but the last few weeks have faded, with price down about 3% over 30 days and CryptoQuant reporting that buying interest has been weak for 12 days in a row (via PANews). Price must win back $81,899 (the 50-day average) before the month leans up again, with room to climb above $86,603 (the 90-day high); winning back that line would be the cue to time bigger campaigns.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 10% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about 35% below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a late-stage run; news is adding a little, as the US bank regulator is inviting community banks to issue stablecoins and holders of tokenized stocks have grown more than tenfold since June (both PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,069 (the 200-day average), with $67,282 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. A close back under the 200-day average would weaken this read and argue for slowing spend on new users.
